built: official birth records only; each place keeps its own publication rules

places.label: the United States
places.dataset: Beyond the Top 1000 Names (national data)
places.rule: Names given to fewer than 5 babies in a year aren't published.

places.label: France
places.dataset: Fichier des prénoms, édition 2024
places.rule: Counts are rounded to the nearest 5. Rare names are grouped and not published. Before 2012, France excluding Mayotte.

places.label: Norway
places.dataset: Table 10467: births by first name
places.rule: Only names used by at least 200 people are listed; fewer than 4 babies in a year aren't published. From 2021, counted by naming year.

places.label: Canada
places.dataset: Table 17-10-0147-01: first names at birth
places.rule: Small counts are suppressed for confidentiality.

places.label: England & Wales
places.dataset: Baby names in England and Wales: 1996 to 2025; Top 100 baby names historical data
places.rule: Names given to 2 or fewer babies are redacted. Spellings are counted separately. 1904–1994: official top 100 every ten years, ranks only.

places.label: Scotland
places.dataset: All names given to babies, 1974 to 2025
places.rule: Every first forename registered.

places.label: Northern Ireland
places.dataset: Baby names full lists
places.rule: Names given to fewer than 3 babies aren't published.

places.label: Ireland
places.dataset: VSA50 / VSA60: names with 3 or more occurrences
places.rule: Names given to fewer than 3 babies aren't published.

places.label: Austria
places.dataset: First names of newborns (OGD)
places.rule: Before 2010 only babies of Austrian nationality were counted; from 2010, all babies.

places.label: New Zealand
places.dataset: Baby name popularity over time
places.rule: Names registered fewer than 10 times in a year aren't published. Years are registration years.

places.label: New South Wales
places.agency: NSW Registry of Births, Deaths & Marriages
places.dataset: Popular baby names from 1952
places.rule: A ranked list of the most popular names only.

places.label: Queensland
places.agency: Queensland Department of Justice (Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages)
places.dataset: Top 100 Baby Names (data.qld.gov.au)
places.rule: Top 100 names only.

places.label: Sweden
places.dataset: TAB619: newborns' 100 most common first names · Namn på nyfödda
places.rule: The name a child is called by (tilltalsnamn). 1998–2022: Statistics Sweden's top 100, with different spellings of a name counted together. From 2023: the Swedish Tax Agency's top list, each spelling counted on its own.

places.label: Poland
places.dataset: Imiona nadawane dzieciom w Polsce (dane.gov.pl)
places.rule: First names of children registered 2000–2025. 2000–2012: names given fewer than 5 times aren't published; from 2013, fewer than 2.

places.label: Denmark
places.dataset: Navne til nyfødte: top 50
places.rule: Top 25 names for 1985–1992, top 50 from 1993; spellings of the same name are counted together. Before 1996 only babies with Danish citizenship were counted.

places.label: Switzerland
places.dataset: DF_BEVNAT_PRENOMS_1 / _2: first names of newborns
places.rule: Every first name given in the latest year, with its count in each year back to 2000; a name nobody was given recently may be missing from earlier years.

places.label: Catalonia
places.dataset: Noms dels nadons
places.rule: Top 100 names of babies born in Catalonia each year. Idescat counts accented and unaccented spellings together (Martí and Marti) and shows one of them.

places.label: Berlin
places.dataset: Liste der häufigen Vornamen
places.rule: One city, not all of Germany (Germany publishes no national list). Babies registered in Berlin. Until 2016 every given name counts; from 2017 only the first name.

places.label: Chile
places.agency: Servicio de Registro Civil e Identificación
places.dataset: Names registered 1920–2021 (via the guaguas dataset)
places.rule: Every first name registered, even once, 1920–2021.

places.label: South Africa
places.dataset: Recorded live births (P0305), top ten baby forenames
places.rule: Top 10 names only, for births that happened and were registered in the year. 2015–2016 count a forename in any position; from 2017 only the first forename.

places.label: Federation of BiH
places.agency: Federal Statistical Office (Federalni zavod za statistiku)
places.dataset: Top 100 names of newborns
places.rule: Top 100 names of babies born in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, one of the country's two entities; Republika Srpska publishes its own list.

places.label: Republika Srpska
places.dataset: Most popular names of newborns
places.rule: Most popular names of babies born in Republika Srpska, one of the country's two entities, ranks only (no counts): top 10 for 2024, top 4 for 2025. Published in Cyrillic and Latin.

places.label: Bulgaria
places.dataset: Names in Bulgaria (annual release)
places.rule: Most common names of babies born in the year: top 20 for 2012–2015, top 10 from 2016 (NSI marks most years preliminary). Names in Latin as NSI writes them in English; the Cyrillic is kept.

places.label: Moldova
places.dataset: Raport statistic privind cel mai frecvent prenume al copiilor nou-născuți (dataset.gov.md)
places.license: Reuse with a link to date.gov.md
places.rule: The most frequent first names of newborns registered by civil-status offices in the year (top 20 in 2018–2022, longer lists in 2016, 2017 and 2023).

places.label: the Netherlands
places.dataset: Kindernamen (child benefit registrations)
places.rule: Children registered for child benefit, by year of birth. Names given to fewer than 10 babies aren't published.

places.label: Luxembourg
places.dataset: La démographie luxembourgeoise en chiffres (top 5 first names of newborns)
places.rule: Top 5 names of all babies born in the year (STATEC also splits them by Luxembourgish and foreign nationality). Tied names share a rank. Spellings are counted separately (Leo and Léo).

places.label: Latvia
places.dataset: 100 most popular newborn names in Latvia
places.rule: Top 100 first names in five-year periods of birth, ranks only (no counts). Each key is the first year of its period (1918 = births 1918–1922); the last period, 2023 to July 2026, is provisional. Before 1990 only people still in the register are counted. Spellings are kept apart (Kristiāns and Kristians).

places.label: Brazil
places.dataset: Censo 2010: Nomes no Brasil
places.rule: Names of people counted in the 2010 census, by the decade they were born; 1920 stands for everyone born before 1930.

places.label: Finland
places.agency: Digital and Population Data Services Agency
places.dataset: Nimipalvelu: suosituimmat etunimet
places.rule: People in the Finnish population register, by the decade they were born, counting every first name a person has (not only the one they go by). Names with fewer than 5 bearers aren't published.

places.label: Spain
places.dataset: Nombres más frecuentes por fecha de nacimiento (Censos de población anuales, 1 January 2025)
places.license: Free reuse citing INE as the source
places.rule: People living in Spain on 1 January 2025, by the decade they were born: the 50 most frequent names of each decade (residents counted, not births; people who died or left before 2025 are missing). 1920 stands for everyone born before 1930; 2020 covers 2020–2024. Compound names count as their own name (María Carmen). INE prints names without accents; they are shown as printed.

places.label: Italy
places.dataset: Conta nomi: names of babies registered at birth (survey Iscritti in anagrafe per nascita)
places.rule: Babies of the resident population registered at birth, by year of birth, from 1999. Every first name is counted, down to one baby, written as ISTAT prints it: compound names whole (Giovanni Pio) and an accented last letter as an apostrophe (Nicolo' for Nicolò). ISTAT does not correct spelling mistakes or a name that doesn't match the baby's sex.

places.label: Türkiye
places.dataset: İstatistiklerle Çocuk (Statistics on Child): most used names of babies born in the year
places.rule: Top 30 names of babies born in the year, from the Address Based Population Registration System (ADNKS). 2014–2020 are ranks only; counts from 2021. 2014 is the age-0 group at the end of the year. Turkish spelling as published (Göktuğ, İnci).

places.label: Taiwan
places.agency: Ministry of the Interior, Department of Household Registration
places.dataset: 全國姓名統計分析 (National name statistics), table 56: top 10 given names by period of birth
places.rule: People in Taiwan's household register on 30 June 2023, by when they were born (ten-year periods counted in Republic of China years: 1912–1920, 1921–1930, and so on; the last is 2021 to June 2023). Living people, not newborn registrations. Names are in Chinese characters as registered; the pinyin for search comes from the CC-CEDICT dictionary, not from the ministry, and is left out where a character has more than one reading.

places.label: Belgium
places.dataset: First names of newborns 1995–2025
places.rule: Statbel publishes names given to at least 5 newborns in a year in Belgium.

places.label: Estonia
places.dataset: Nimede statistika: popular first names by year of birth (population register, 1 January 2026)
places.rule: People in the Estonian population register on 1 January 2026, by the five-year period they were born (living residents, not newborn registrations), top 10 per period with counts; tied names share a rank. Statistics Estonia also lists everyone born up to 1935 as one group, left out here.

places.label: Serbia
places.agency: Statistical Office of the Republic of Serbia (RZS)
places.dataset: Census 2022: Најчешћа имена и презимена (Most common names and surnames), tables 1–2
places.rule: People counted in the 2022 census (30 September 2022), by the decade they were born; the last period runs 2011–2022. Ranks only (top 10, no counts). RZS prints the names in Cyrillic; the Latin is Serbia's own Latin alphabet, which matches Cyrillic letter for letter. People born in 1940 or earlier form one group, left out here. No census was held in Kosovo.

places.label: Slovenia
places.agency: Statistical Office of the Republic of Slovenia (SURS)
places.dataset: SiStat 05X2001S / 05X2002S: names of newborn boys and girls
places.rule: Names of babies born in Slovenia, in their legal form from the Central Population Register, top 20 with SURS's own ranks. SURS lists a name only if at least 5 babies got it in some year (6 for 1992–1998).

places.label: Hungary
places.agency: Ministry of the Interior, Deputy State Secretariat for Registers
places.dataset: A 100 leggyakrabban választott utónév (the 100 most chosen first names of children born the previous year)
places.rule: Top names of children born in the year, counted by their first given name in the personal-data and address register on 1 January of the next year. The ministry prints names in capitals; they are shown in ordinary case.

places.label: Czechia
places.dataset: Nejoblíbenější dětská jména (most popular children's names), from the Basic Population Register
places.rule: Top 20 names of children born in Czechia, from the population register (ČSÚ calls the results indicative). Ranks only until 2024; counts from 2025. Each spelling counts on its own. 2010–2021 are read from the table in ČSÚ's 2026 presentation; 2022–2025 from its TOP 100 files.

places.label: Portugal
places.agency: Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado (IRN)
places.dataset: Registo de Nomes: top 20 nomes próprios registados (dados.gov.pt)
places.rule: The 20 first names registered most often in Portugal each year, as the registry (IRN) publishes them; IRN doesn't say whether only babies' first names are counted.

places.label: Victoria
places.dataset: Popular Baby Names (DataVic)
places.rule: Top 100 names of births registered in Victoria each year.

places.label: Western Australia
places.agency: WA Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages (Department of Justice)
places.dataset: Popular baby names, from the Registry's yearly announcements on wa.gov.au
places.rule: Births registered in Western Australia. Only the Registry's own announcements are still online: the top 3 for 2013, the top 20 with counts for 2015 (from its top-50 table) and the top 10 as ranks for 2019–2025; 2014 and 2016–2018 aren't published anywhere. Tied names share a rank.

places.label: South Korea
places.agency: Supreme Court of Korea (family relationship registration)
places.dataset: 상위 출생신고 이름 현황 (top names in birth registrations), family registration statistics
places.rule: Top 20 given names in birth registrations, by year of registration (late registrations of earlier births included), from 2008 when the family-relationship register began; the court calls the figures provisional. Names are registered in Hangul; the Latin is the Revised Romanization, syllable by syllable, as it is used for given names.

places.label: Jewish
places.dataset: Current first names of people born 1949–2024, by sex and population group (media release 391/2025, table 1)
places.rule: Jewish babies in Israel, by year of birth, counted by the first name they hold today (so a name changed later counts under the new one); small counts are suppressed. CBS publishes each population group on its own; they are kept apart here. CBS writes every name in Hebrew letters (Arab names too); a name is shown in Latin letters only where its usual spelling is known, otherwise as CBS writes it.

places.label: Muslim
places.dataset: Current first names of people born 1949–2024, by sex and population group (media release 391/2025, table 1)
places.rule: Muslim babies in Israel, by year of birth, counted by the first name they hold today (so a name changed later counts under the new one); small counts are suppressed. CBS publishes each population group on its own; they are kept apart here. CBS writes every name in Hebrew letters (Arab names too); a name is shown in Latin letters only where its usual spelling is known, otherwise as CBS writes it.

places.label: Christian Arab
places.dataset: Current first names of people born 1949–2024, by sex and population group (media release 391/2025, table 1)
places.rule: Christian Arab babies in Israel, by year of birth, counted by the first name they hold today (so a name changed later counts under the new one); small counts are suppressed. CBS publishes each population group on its own; they are kept apart here. CBS writes every name in Hebrew letters (Arab names too); a name is shown in Latin letters only where its usual spelling is known, otherwise as CBS writes it.

places.label: Druze
places.dataset: Current first names of people born 1949–2024, by sex and population group (media release 391/2025, table 1)
places.rule: Druze babies in Israel, by year of birth, counted by the first name they hold today (so a name changed later counts under the new one); small counts are suppressed. CBS publishes each population group on its own; they are kept apart here. CBS writes every name in Hebrew letters (Arab names too); a name is shown in Latin letters only where its usual spelling is known, otherwise as CBS writes it.

places.label: Tunisia
places.dataset: Les prénoms des nouveau-nés les plus populaires (press release, 29 December 2023), from the civil-status registers
places.rule: Top 10 names of newborns for 1922, every tenth year from 1950 to 2020, 2021 and 2022, with counts (1922 as ranks only), in INS's own Latin spelling. The 2010 boys' list is left out: INS printed the 2020 list in its place.

places.label: Curaçao
places.agency: Central Bureau of Statistics Curaçao (data: Kranshi population register)
places.dataset: Most popular names in Curaçao, by age and gender (2018)
places.license: Free to use citing CBS Curaçao
places.rule: People in Curaçao's population register in 2018, by age group turned into years of birth (0–14 = 2004–2018 and so on), top 20 with counts. Living residents, not newborn registrations; the 65-and-over group is left out because it has no first year.

places.label: Philippines
places.dataset: Most common baby names, from registered live births (via the Wayback Machine; psa.gov.ph blocks scripts)
places.rule: Registered live births, exact first names, not adjusted for late registration: top 20 for 2005, top 10 for 2014, 2015, 2017, 2018 and 2020–2023, with counts. 2016 and 2019 weren't published online.

places.label: Montevideo
places.dataset: Partidas de Registro Civil de Montevideo: nombre_nacim_x_anio_sexo (catalogodatos.gub.uy)
places.license: Licencia de Datos Abiertos de Uruguay
places.rule: Births registered in Montevideo by year, sex and first name, 1940–2012 (one department, about 40% of Uruguay's births; no national list exists). Top 20 shown. Names as registered, without accents; 2012 is missing November and December.

places.label: Jordan
places.dataset: Annual reports: most frequent names of newborns by sex and year of birth (2015–2024)
places.rule: Births registered in Jordan by year of birth, top 20 with counts. CSPD prints names in Arabic; a name is shown in Latin letters only where its usual spelling is known, otherwise as CSPD writes it, and two printed spellings of one name (احمد, أحمد) stay apart.

places.label: Croatia
places.agency: Ministry of Justice, Administration and Digital Transformation (birth register)
places.dataset: Statistički prikaz, table 2: the 50 most frequent names of children born in the year
places.rule: Top names of children born in Croatia each year, 2021–2025, with counts (top 20 shown of the ministry's 50). Names in capitals in the source, shown in ordinary case.

places.label: Liechtenstein
places.dataset: Neugeborenennamen (names of newborns), publication 261
places.rule: Names of babies born in Liechtenstein (about 350 a year), names given at least twice, 2018–2022; for 2023–2024 only the few names the office announced. The office groups spellings that sound alike (Sofia, Sophia).

places.label: Greece
places.dataset: 2021 Census: most common names by year of birth (poster)
places.rule: People counted in the 2021 census (born in Greece, Greek citizens), by decade of birth, top 10, ranks only (ELSTAT gives percentages, not counts). Names are printed in Greek capitals; the Latin is ELOT 743, the system on Greek passports.

places.label: Kazakhstan
places.dataset: Popular names among newborns (Популярные имена service)
places.rule: Top 20 names of newborns in Kazakhstan each year, 1990–2025, with counts. The bureau prints names in Cyrillic; the Latin is the site's known spelling where it has one, otherwise BGN/PCGN.

places.label: Armenia
places.dataset: Names most often given to newborns, by sex (appendix to the annual Socio-Economic Situation report)
places.rule: Top names of newborns in Armenia each year, 2008–2025, with counts (top 20 shown). Armstat prints the names in Armenian script; the Latin is the site's known spelling where it has one, otherwise BGN/PCGN as on Armenian passports.

places.label: Kyrgyzstan
places.dataset: TOP-10 popular names of girls and boys (data.gov.kg)
places.rule: Top 10 names given in Kyrgyzstan in 2023, with counts. Names in Cyrillic in the source; the Latin is the site's known spelling where it has one, otherwise BGN/PCGN. Spellings are kept apart (Мухаммад, Мухаммед).

places.label: Rwanda
places.agency: National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda (CRVS)
places.dataset: Rwanda Vital Statistics Report, annex: top 20 most preferred babies' Kinyarwanda names
places.rule: The child's own Kinyarwanda name (what NISR calls a surname, though it isn't a family name), for births registered in the same year, 2020–2025, with counts; Christian or other first names aren't in these tables. Some years in NISR's own tables look misprinted (2021 girls); they're kept as printed.

places.label: Wales
places.dataset: Baby names in England and Wales, table 3: top names for babies in Wales
places.rule: Live births registered in the year whose mother usually lives in Wales, 1997–2025, with counts (top 20 shown). The England & Wales place counts both together.

places.label: Newborns
places.dataset: Nacimientos según el nombre del nacido (births by the baby's name)
places.rule: Babies born in Spain each year, 2002–2024, with counts (top 20 shown). Unlike the Spain place built from residents, these are births. INE prints names in capitals without accents.

places.label: Population
places.dataset: Ranks of names by age group, 1 January 2023 (MAN11105, MAN11115)
places.rule: People living in Iceland on 1 January 2023, by five-year group of birth (ranks only, top 20); older groups are survivors only and every group includes immigrants. A population snapshot, not births.

places.label: Newborns
places.dataset: Vinsælustu nöfnin (the most popular names of newborns)
places.rule: First given names of babies born in 2021 and 2022, with counts. Later years are published only as charts that don't separate girls and boys.

places.label: Malay
places.dataset: Baby Name Popularity dashboard
places.rule: Living Malaysians in the identity-card register, by decade of birth (1940s–2010s), top 10 with counts. JPN lists Malay, Chinese and Indian names separately and never combined; kept apart here. Names are lower case in the source.

places.label: Chinese
places.dataset: Baby Name Popularity dashboard
places.rule: Living Malaysians in the identity-card register, by decade of birth, top 10 with counts. The 1940s and 1950s are left out: their lists are mostly surnames, from the order of names on old ID records.

places.label: Indian
places.dataset: Baby Name Popularity dashboard
places.rule: Living Malaysians in the identity-card register, by decade of birth (1940s–2010s), top 10 with counts.
